title.en: I did it myself; we know each other

goal.sl: Poveš, kdaj kdo dela kaj sebi ali sam (I cut myself, I did it myself), kdaj je kdo sam (on my own), kdaj drug drugemu (each other), in rabiš one in ones.
goal.de: Du sagst, wann jemand etwas sich selbst tut oder selbst macht (I cut myself, I did it myself), wann jemand allein ist (on my own), wann einander (each other), und verwendest one und ones.
goal.it: Dici quando qualcuno fa qualcosa a se stesso o da solo (I cut myself, I did it myself), quando è solo (on my own), quando l'un l'altro (each other), e usi one e ones.
goal.en: You can say when people do something to themselves or with no help (I cut myself, I did it myself), when they're alone (on my own), when both ways (each other), and use one and ones.

say.sl: Kdor dela, je tudi tisti, ki se mu zgodi: **I cut myself.** (Urezal{m:|f:a} sem se.) **Alfie hurt himself.** (Alfie se je poškodoval.) **Did you enjoy yourselves?** Slovenščina ima za vse *se*, angleščina eno obliko za vsako osebo: **myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves**.
say.de: Wer es tut, dem geschieht es auch: **I cut myself.** (Ich habe mich geschnitten.) **Alfie hurt himself.** (Alfie hat sich wehgetan.) **Did you enjoy yourselves?** Es gibt eine Form je Person: **myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves**.
say.it: Chi fa la cosa è anche chi la riceve: **I cut myself.** (Mi sono tagliat{m:o|f:a}.) **Alfie hurt himself.** (Alfie si è fatto male.) **Did you enjoy yourselves?** C'è una forma per ogni persona: **myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves**.
say.en: The one who does it is the one it happens to: **I cut myself.** **Alfie hurt himself.** **Did you enjoy yourselves?** There is one form for each person: **myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves**.

say.sl: Ista beseda pove, da nekdo dela sam, brez pomoči: **I did it myself.** (Naredil{m:|f:a} sem sam{m:|f:a}.) **Mrs Birkett bakes the bread herself.** **Did you make it yourself?** Ljudje rečejo tudi *hisself*, *theirselves*, na severu *meself*; pisava hoče **himself**, **themselves**, **myself**.
say.de: Dasselbe Wort sagt, dass jemand es selbst tut, ohne Hilfe: **I did it myself.** (Ich habe es selbst gemacht.) **Mrs Birkett bakes the bread herself.** **Did you make it yourself?** Man sagt auch *hisself*, *theirselves*, im Norden *meself*; geschrieben steht **himself**, **themselves**, **myself**.
say.it: La stessa parola dice che qualcuno lo fa da solo, senza aiuto: **I did it myself.** (L'ho fatto da sol{m:o|f:a}.) **Mrs Birkett bakes the bread herself.** **Did you make it yourself?** Si dice anche *hisself*, *theirselves*, al nord *meself*; per iscritto si usa **himself**, **themselves**, **myself**.
say.en: The same word says someone does it with no help: **I did it myself.** **Mrs Birkett bakes the bread herself.** **Did you make it yourself?** People also say *hisself*, *theirselves*, and in the North *meself*; writing wants **himself**, **themselves**, **myself**.

examples.it: Mrs Birkett fa il pane da sola.

say.sl: Mnogi slovenski povratni glagoli v angleščini nimajo besede za *se*: **I feel tired.** (Počutim se utrujen{m:|f:a}.) **We met at the inn.** (Srečali smo se v gostilni.) **I remember.** (Spomnim se.) **Sit down.** **Hurry up.** **He washed and went out.** Ampak **enjoy** jo rabi: **Enjoy yourself!** (Uživaj!)
say.de: Viele deutsche reflexive Verben haben im Englischen kein *sich*: **I feel tired.** (Ich fühle mich müde.) **We met at the inn.** (Wir haben uns im Gasthaus getroffen.) **I remember.** (Ich erinnere mich.) **Sit down.** **Hurry up.** **He washed and went out.** Aber **enjoy** braucht es: **Enjoy yourself!** (Viel Spaß!)
say.it: Molti riflessivi italiani in inglese non hanno il *si*: **I feel tired.** (Mi sento stanc{m:o|f:a}.) **We met at the inn.** (Ci siamo incontrati alla locanda.) **I remember.** (Mi ricordo.) **Sit down.** **Hurry up.** **He washed and went out.** Ma **enjoy** ne ha bisogno: **Enjoy yourself!** (Divertiti!)
say.en: Many verbs don't take it: **I feel tired.** **We met at the inn.** **I remember.** **Sit down.** **Hurry up.** **He washed and went out.** But **enjoy** needs it: **Enjoy yourself!**

say.sl: **on my own** in **by myself** pomenita sam, brez drugih: **I live on my own.** (Živim sam{m:|f:a}.) **Old Wilf lives on his own.** **Jack works by himself.** **Did you come on your own?** **alone** pove isto. Rabiš **on** + my, his, her + **own**, ali **by** + myself, himself.
say.de: **on my own** und **by myself** heißen allein: **I live on my own.** (Ich lebe allein.) **Old Wilf lives on his own.** **Jack works by himself.** **Did you come on your own?** **alone** sagt dasselbe. Du brauchst **on** + my, his, her + **own** oder **by** + myself, himself.
say.it: **on my own** e **by myself** vogliono dire da solo, senza altri: **I live on my own.** (Vivo da sol{m:o|f:a}.) **Old Wilf lives on his own.** **Jack works by himself.** **Did you come on your own?** **alone** dice lo stesso. Ti serve **on** + my, his, her + **own**, o **by** + myself, himself.
say.en: **on my own** and **by myself** say alone: **I live on my own.** **Old Wilf lives on his own.** **Jack works by himself.** **Did you come on your own?** **alone** says the same. It's **on** + my, his, her + **own**, or **by** + myself, himself.

examples.en: Old Wilf lives on his own.
examples.it: Il vecchio Wilf vive da solo.

say.sl: **each other** gre v obe smeri, drug drugega: **Jack and Sam know each other.** (Jack in Sam se poznata.) **We phone each other on Sundays.** **themselves** obrne vsakega nase: **They looked at themselves in the water.** (Gledali so se v vodi.) Slovenski *se* je oboje. Tudi **one another** je pravilno.
say.de: **each other** geht in beide Richtungen, einander: **Jack and Sam know each other.** (Jack und Sam kennen sich.) **We phone each other on Sundays.** **themselves** wendet jeden auf sich selbst: **They looked at themselves in the water.** (Sie haben sich im Wasser angeschaut.) Deutsches *sich* ist beides. Auch **one another** ist richtig.
say.it: **each other** va nei due sensi, l'un l'altro: **Jack and Sam know each other.** (Jack e Sam si conoscono.) **We phone each other on Sundays.** **themselves** riporta ognuno su se stesso: **They looked at themselves in the water.** (Si sono guardati nell'acqua.) L'italiano *si* è tutti e due. Anche **one another** è giusto.
say.en: **each other** goes both ways: **Jack and Sam know each other.** **We phone each other on Sundays.** **themselves** turns back on each one: **They looked at themselves in the water.** **one another** is right too.

examples.en: Jack and Sam know each other.
We phone each other on Sundays.
examples.de: Am Sonntag rufen wir einander an.

examples.en: They looked at themselves in the water.
examples.de: Sie haben sich im Wasser angeschaut.

say.sl: **one** stoji namesto samostalnika, ki ga že poznaš, **ones** v množini: **Which coat? The red one.** (Kateri plašč? Rdečega.) **I like the big ones.** (Rad{m:|f:a} imam velike.) **This one or that one?** **My boots are old. I need new ones.** Slovenščina reče samo *rdečega*, angleščina potrebuje **one**.
say.de: **one** steht für ein Nomen, das du schon kennst, **ones** im Plural: **Which coat? The red one.** (Welcher Mantel? Der rote.) **I like the big ones.** (Ich mag die großen.) **This one or that one?** **My boots are old. I need new ones.** Deutsch sagt nur *der rote*, Englisch braucht **one**.
say.it: **one** sta per un nome già noto, **ones** al plurale: **Which coat? The red one.** (Quale cappotto? Quello rosso.) **I like the big ones.** (Mi piacciono quelli grandi.) **This one or that one?** **My boots are old. I need new ones.** L'italiano dice *quello rosso*, l'inglese ha bisogno di **one**.
say.en: **one** stands for a noun you've already named, **ones** for a plural: **Which coat? The red one.** **I like the big ones.** **This one or that one?** **My boots are old. I need new ones.** After an adjective English needs it.

rows: the red one, the big ones

translation.sl: Alfie je padel z zidu in se poškodoval. Poppy se je urezala ob pločevinko. »Sta se imela lepo na plesu?« je vprašala gospa Hartley. »O ja, zelo lepo sva se imela!« Pa vrata? Odprla so se sama.
translation.de: Alfie ist von der Mauer gefallen und hat sich wehgetan. Poppy hat sich an einer Dose geschnitten. „Habt ihr euch beim Tanz gut unterhalten?“, fragte Mrs Hartley. „O ja, sehr gut!“ Und das Tor? Das ist von selbst aufgegangen.
translation.it: Alfie è caduto dal muro e si è fatto male. Poppy si è tagliata con una lattina. «Vi siete divertiti al ballo, voi due?» ha chiesto Mrs Hartley. «Oh sì, ci siamo divertiti molto!» E il cancello? Si è aperto da solo.
translation.en: Alfie fell off the wall and hurt himself. Poppy cut herself on a tin. "Did you enjoy yourselves at the dance, you two?" asked Mrs Hartley. "Oh yes, we enjoyed ourselves very much!" And the gate? It opened by itself.

translation.sl: Stari Wilf živi sam. Rad je sam. Sam si je naredil stol in sam se striže. »Skuhal{m:|f:a} sem si skodelico čaja,« sem mu rekel{m:|f:la}, »in bil je prevroč!«
translation.de: Der alte Wilf lebt allein. Er ist gern für sich. Er hat sich einen Sessel gemacht, und er schneidet sich die Haare selbst. „Ich habe mir eine Tasse Tee gemacht“, sagte ich zu ihm, „und er war zu heiß!“
translation.it: Il vecchio Wilf vive da solo. Gli piace stare da solo. Si è fatto una sedia e si taglia i capelli da solo. «Mi sono fatt{m:o|f:a} una tazza di tè», gli ho detto, «ed era troppo caldo!»
translation.en: Old Wilf lives on his own. He likes being by himself. He made himself a chair, and he cuts his hair himself. "I made myself a cup of tea," I told him, "and it was too hot!"

exercises.text: Mr Tyson mended the wheel ___. He cut ___ on the saw. "Be careful!" said his wife. They've known ___ for forty years. He likes working on his ___. But today he needs a new saw: the old ___ is broken.

translation.sl: Gospod Tyson je sam popravil kolo. Urezal se je z žago. »Pazi!« je rekla žena. Poznata se že štirideset let. Rad dela sam. Danes pa potrebuje novo žago: stara je zlomljena.
translation.de: Mr Tyson hat das Rad selbst repariert. Er hat sich an der Säge geschnitten. „Pass auf!“, sagte seine Frau. Sie kennen sich seit vierzig Jahren. Er arbeitet gern allein. Aber heute braucht er eine neue Säge: Die alte ist kaputt.
translation.it: Mr Tyson ha riparato la ruota da solo. Si è tagliato con la sega. «Stai attento!» ha detto sua moglie. Si conoscono da quarant'anni. Gli piace lavorare da solo. Ma oggi gli serve una sega nuova: quella vecchia è rotta.
translation.en: Mr Tyson mended the wheel himself. He cut himself on the saw. "Be careful!" said his wife. They've known each other for forty years. He likes working on his own. But today he needs a new saw: the old one is broken.
